notes: **Format.** A formal email has the recipient's address, a clear subject line, a salutation, a concise body and a closing with the sender's name and designation.
**Subject line.** The subject states the purpose in a few precise words so the reader knows the request before opening the message.
**Tone.** Formal emails use complete sentences and polite requests; informal emails to friends may use contractions and a casual tone.
**Body.** Open with the purpose, develop one or two short paragraphs of essential detail, and end with the action you want — a reply, a meeting or confirmation.
**Netiquette.** Keep the message brief, avoid slang and all-capital text, use CC and BCC appropriately, and recheck names and addresses before sending.
